title: Feature Request, Add optional Right Mouse Button hold as activation modifier for Grab and Move
author: kjmdjul

status.label: Needs interaction details
status.detail: The mouse-only goal is clear, but the requested right-button modifier conflicts with the existing right-button resize gesture and does not define how move versus resize would be selected.

next_action.label: Clarify the mouse-only gesture
next_action.reason: Ask for the exact button chords and context-menu behavior needed before evaluating a safe input-hook design.

judgment.rationale: The report establishes the accessibility/productivity goal but leaves the core gesture contract ambiguous: right-click is already the resize button while Alt or Win is held, so using it as the modifier does not specify separate move and resize gestures.
evidence: The reporter requests an optional right-mouse-button hold modifier with normal right-click suppressed only during the gesture.
Grab and Move currently supports only Alt and Win activation modifiers in src/modules/GrabAndMove/GrabAndMove/main.cpp.
The current mouse hook uses modifier + left button for moving and modifier + right button for resizing, so the proposed modifier overlaps an existing action.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask the reporter to define the intended move and resize button chords, release behavior, and when a normal context menu should still be delivered.

issue_context.summary: A mouse-only Grab and Move mode is requested, using a held right mouse button instead of Alt or Win while suppressing the ordinary context-menu click during an active gesture.
known_information: The requested mode is optional and intended to preserve the existing Alt and Win choices.
The desired workflow is one-handed window moving and resizing with only the mouse.
Current Grab and Move code maps modifier + left button to move and modifier + right button to resize.
inferences: A right-button modifier may be feasible, but it would require a new unambiguous chord/state model because the same button currently selects resize.
issue_context.analysis: The use case is concrete, but implementation cannot be designed safely until the interaction distinguishes move, resize, cancellation, and an ordinary right-click. Those choices determine hook suppression and replay behavior and would materially change the design.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue and its only triage comment; no linked implementation or assignee is present.
Inspected src/modules/GrabAndMove/GrabAndMove/main.cpp: GrabAndMoveModifier contains Alt/Win choices, and the hook separately handles modifier + left/right button.
Issues #47429 and #49044 request Right Alt support, not a mouse-button activation contract, so they are related but not duplicates.

information_gaps.information: The exact mouse chords for move and resize, including what happens when the right button is released first.
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether the proposal can coexist with the existing right-button resize action without ambiguous or stuck input state.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with a short numbered gesture sequence for move and resize.

information_gaps.information: When a normal right-click/context menu should be replayed instead of starting Grab and Move.
information_gaps.why_needed: The hook must know when suppressing the click is intended and when the target application must receive it.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Describe the cancel/no-drag case and any hold threshold you expect.

actions.label: Clarify mouse-only gesture

comment.body: Thanks for describing the mouse-only goal and the need to preserve the existing Alt/Win options. One interaction detail is still needed before this can be designed: Grab and Move currently uses modifier + left button to move and modifier + right button to resize, so making right button the modifier overlaps the resize gesture. Could you give numbered button sequences for both move and resize, including what should happen if the right button is released before any drag, and when a normal right-click/context menu should still be delivered?

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream comment is posted without explicit approval.
